claims.text: Stainless steel exhibits reduced corrosion resistance under extreme and aggressive corrosive conditions.
Laser cladding can deposit a high-entropy alloy coating on a steel surface.
A high-entropy alloy coating can be deposited by laser cladding specifically on stainless steel.
A machine-learning framework can optimize laser power, scanning speed, energy input, and post-deposition heat treatment for high-entropy alloy laser cladding.
Machine-learning optimization of laser cladding parameters improves the corrosion resistance of the resulting coating.
High-temperature molten salts are relevant corrosive environments for high-entropy alloys and stainless steels in advanced energy applications, including nuclear energy.
The proposed treatment is applicable to aggressive oxidizing atmospheres typical of aerospace applications.
Laser cladding produces a dense, fine-grained high-entropy alloy surface layer with controlled microstructure.
Increasing chromium content in a laser-clad refractory high-entropy alloy coating refines its grains.
The controlled coating microstructure promotes protective, self-healing oxide films enriched in corrosion-resistant elements.
A machine-learning model can use prior laser-cladding data to predict optimal deposition parameters.
Machine-learning-selected deposition parameters enhance the coating microstructure.
The enhanced coating microstructure accelerates formation of protective oxide layers.
Protective oxide layers act as diffusion barriers and thereby mitigate corrosive attack on the stainless-steel substrate.
A high-entropy alloy can have a substantially lower molten-salt corrosion rate than duplex stainless steel.
Machine-learning-optimized high-entropy alloy coatings on stainless steel will have a significantly lower corrosion rate than untreated stainless steel.
Machine-learning-optimized coatings will outperform coatings produced by non-optimized, trial-and-error laser cladding.
The effectiveness of the machine-learning predictions depends on the quality and range of the training data and may decline outside the training conditions.

contradictions.description: The baseline, predicted outcome, and falsification rule require comparison with both untreated stainless steel and non-optimized coatings, but the experimental design prepares only two coated sets and does not include an untreated stainless-steel group.
